name: MathlibAnnex.Matrix.maximalMinors_mul
title: Right multiplication scales every maximal minor by one determinant

content.display_title: Right multiplication scales every maximal minor by one determinant
content.one_sentence_role: Turns a square right factor into a common scalar on the family of maximal minors.
content.natural_language_statement:
For an $I$-by-$n$ matrix $A$ and an $n$-by-$n$ matrix $L$ over a commutative ring, with $I$ linearly ordered, write $\mathcal M(A)$ for the family of determinants of all $n$-row submatrices in increasing row order. Then

$$\mathcal M(AL)=(\det L)\,\mathcal M(A).$$

The equality is pointwise on $n$-element row subsets, using increasing row order on both sides.
content.assumptions: The integer $n$ may be zero; the row set may be infinite. The coefficient ring is commutative. The square factor $L$ need not be invertible.
content.conclusion: For each selected subset $S$, $\det((AL)_S)=(\det L)\det(A_S)$. Thus one scalar, independent of $S$, scales the whole family.
content.proof_summary: Select the same rows before and after multiplication, then apply multiplicativity of the square determinant.

proof_steps.text: For an $n$-element subset $S$, matrix multiplication is a sum over the finite column set. Hence selecting rows commutes with that sum: $(AL)_S=A_SL$.

Both selected matrices are square over a commutative ring, so determinant multiplicativity applies:

$$\mathcal M(AL)(S)=\det(A_SL)=\det(A_S)\det L=(\det L)\mathcal M(A)(S).$$

Commutativity gives the scalar in the stated order. Since this holds for every $S$, the two functions are equal. For $n=0$ the same calculation reads $1=1\cdot1$.

content.lean_realization_notes: Related identities in the same source distinguish scalar multiplication from right multiplication: $\mathcal M(cA)=c^n\mathcal M(A)$. The zero-matrix family vanishes when $n>0$; this restriction matters, because the empty determinant for $n=0$ is $1$. Selection commutes also with application to a column vector: $(Av)|_S=A_Sv$. These are separate identities, not invertibility assumptions for the displayed theorem.
